intro: Social media manager client onboarding is often the most fragmented part of your week. You spend hours chasing passwords, brand assets, and approval chains before you even create a single post.

blocks.text: Why social media manager client onboarding fails

The failure in onboarding usually stems from a lack of structure. You likely rely on scattered emails to gather logins and brand assets. This forces you to switch contexts constantly. Every time you switch from your creative work to an administrative email, you lose focus. Research shows it takes 23 minutes to regain deep focus after an interruption. If you do this ten times a day, you lose nearly four hours of potential work time.
Fixing the onboarding process on your Mac

items: Create a standard intake form using Typeform or Google Forms. Never ask for assets via email threads.
Use a shared cloud folder for every new client. Link this in your first onboarding email.
Use Chrome profiles to keep client logins separate. This prevents you from posting to the wrong account.
Set up a dedicated Notion page for each client. This acts as your single source of truth for passwords and brand guidelines.

blocks.text: Poor onboarding costs you more than just time. It creates friction that damages your relationship with the client. When you spend the first month just trying to get access to accounts, the client feels like you are not working. This leads to early churn. Replacing a client is significantly more expensive than retaining one. You also deal with the mental toll of managing disjointed communications.

Security is part of the onboarding process. Never ask clients to email you their passwords. Use a password manager like 1Password or Bitwarden. If you must use shared access, use the platform's native collaborator features. For example, add yourself as an editor on their Facebook page rather than logging in as them. This protects their data and keeps your activity logs clean.
If you work for a company, always follow your employer's rules regarding client data. Never store sensitive login credentials in unencrypted text files or personal notes.
blocks.title: Security first

faq.question: How can I automate client onboarding emails?
faq.answer: Use templates in your email client. When a client signs, you can use Lazur to draft a personalized welcome message that includes links to your intake form and shared folder.

faq.question: Should I use a different browser for each client?
faq.answer: Yes. Using Chrome profiles or separate browser instances keeps cookies and logins isolated. This prevents you from accidentally posting content to the wrong brand account.

faq.question: What if a client refuses to use my onboarding process?
faq.answer: Explain that the process is designed to save them money by reducing billable hours spent on administrative tasks. If they still refuse, you may need to adjust your pricing to cover the extra manual work.
